1.title: Zip Up the Tent!
1.topic: camping with Mom: setting up a tent, a campfire hot dog and stars at night (family, outdoors, nature)
sounds: '에'를 짧고 가볍게: red '렏', set '셑'. 길게 끌지 않아요.
입을 옆으로 크게 벌려 '애': camp '캠프'가 아니라 '캠p'.
끝소리 t, p에 '으'를 붙이지 말고 입만 닫아요: tent '텐트' ✗ → '텐t' ○.
1.expression: Sound excited about camping, make “Snap! Pop!” crackle like a real fire, point up and wonder on “Can you see the stars?” with your voice going up, then whisper a soft, sleepy “Good night!”

2.title: Theo's First Steps
2.topic: a big sister helps her baby brother take his first steps at home (family, growing up, feelings)
lines: Theo *landed* in Ana's arms, | and she *hugged* him *tight*.
sounds: l, b, n, g 뒤 -ed는 약한 d: pulled '풀드', hugged '허그드'.
t·d 뒤는 '이드'(wanted '원티드'), p·k 뒤는 짧은 t(walked '웍트', l은 소리 안 나요).
One step, ↗ two steps, ↗ three steps! ↘
숫자에 힘을 주고 한 박자씩, 마지막 three steps에서 크게 내려요.
2.expression: Read it like a proud big sister: gentle at the start, a funny little “Uh-oh!” with a giggle, warm and inviting on “Come here, Theo!”, count the steps slowly with growing excitement, then shout “Theo walked!” with joy.

3.title: Super Penguin Dads
3.topic: how emperor penguin fathers keep their eggs warm through the Antarctic winter (animals, science, family)
lines: Then she *carefully* *passes* the egg | to the *father*.
The mother walks to the *sea* | to *eat* *fish*. | She will be *gone* | for about *two* *months*!
The dad *holds* the egg | on *top* of his *feet*.
A *warm* *flap* of *skin* | *covers* the egg | like a *cozy* *blanket*.
The *wind* *howls*, | and the *snow* *blows*. | How do the dads stay *warm*? ↘
At *last*, | the egg *hatches*, | and the mother *comes* *back*.
sounds: 힘주는 음절을 크고 길게. Antarctica는 두 번째 ARC에 힘을 줘요.
혀끝을 윗니와 아랫니 사이에 살짝 물고 목을 울려요: '더'가 아니라 'th-'.
s, ch 소리 뒤 -es는 '이즈': passes '패시즈', hatches '해치즈'.
3.expression: Read it like a nature-show host: clear and amazed for the facts, a little dramatic on “She will be gone for about two months!”, cold and windy on “The wind howls,” curious on the How question, and cheerful and proud on “Mom will! It's her turn now.”

4.title: The Talent Show Juggler
4.topic: a boy practices juggling for the school talent show, drops a beanbag on stage, makes a joke and tries again (school, performing, feelings, mistakes)
lines: Every *night*, | he *tossed* three *bright* *beanbags* | *higher* and *higher* in his *bedroom*.
On the night of the *show*, | Owen *peeked* out | from *behind* the *curtain*.
His *heart* *pounded* like a *drum*. | “What if I *mess* *up*?” | he *whispered*.
Owen *walked* to the *middle* of the *stage* | and *started* to *juggle*.
Then he *grinned*, | *picked* it *up*, | and said, | “*Oops*! | That one *needed* a *nap*.”
He *tried* *again*. | This time, | the beanbags *danced* | in a *perfect* *circle*.
The crowd *cheered*. | Owen *bowed* and *smiled*. | *Mistakes* can *happen*, | but you can *always* *try* *again*. ↘
sounds: 첫 음절에 힘을 주고 나머지는 약하게. rhythm은 '리듬'이 아니라 'RHY-thm' 두 박자.
practiced, peeked, slipped / squeezed, cheered / pounded, started
s·k·p 뒤는 t(peeked '픽트'), z·r 뒤는 d, t·d 뒤는 '이드'(pounded '파운디드').
단어를 이어서 한 덩어리로: picked it up → 'pick-ti-dup'. 끊지 말고 미끄러지듯 연결해요.
4.expression: Tell it like a storyteller on stage: steady and determined for the practice, quick and bouncy on “toss, catch,” nervous and quiet on “What if I mess up?”, warm and sure on “You've got this,” freeze on the silent moment, then playful on “That one needed a nap,” and finish with a proud, encouraging last line.
practice: Mistakes can happen, but you can always try again.
